# Reproducible figures — original project workbooks

The figures appear once each, in the same order as Appendix A.3 (A.11–A.21)
and Appendix B.2 (B.11–B.22). All observational values are loaded from the
existing Excel workbooks in the RStudio project folder. The code does not rely
on supplementary/manual tables. The article contribution workbook must be the
**updated** version derived from Tables 4.1–4.5 of the dissertation; older
versions produce different counts.

```{r setup, include=FALSE, fig.align="center"}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  dev = "png",
  dpi = 150
)

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(forcats)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(ggrepel)
library(patchwork)
library(wordcloud)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)
library(grid)

# The project contains the original Excel workbooks alongside this Rmd.
project_file <- function(candidates, description) {
  present <- candidates[file.exists(candidates)]
  if (length(present) == 0L) {
    stop(paste0("Missing source workbook for ", description, ": ",
                paste(candidates, collapse = " or ")))
  }
  present[[1]]
}

# Prefer named columns; normalize punctuation/case/diacritics for robustness.
normalized_header <- function(x) {
  x <- iconv(as.character(x), to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT")
  x[is.na(x)] <- ""
  x <- tolower(x)
  x <- gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "_", x)
  gsub("^_|_$", "", x)
}

project_columns <- function(df, candidates, description) {
  original <- names(df)
  normalized <- normalized_header(original)
  candidate_norm <- normalized_header(candidates)
  hits <- which(normalized %in% candidate_norm)
  if (length(hits) == 0L) {
    stop(paste0("Missing column for ", description,
                ". Accepted: ", paste(candidates, collapse = ", "),
                ". Available: ", paste(original, collapse = ", ")))
  }
  original[hits[[1]]]
}

read_project_sheet <- function(file, preferred_sheet = NULL) {
  sheets <- readxl::excel_sheets(file)
  if (is.null(preferred_sheet)) {
    return(readxl::read_excel(file, sheet = 1))
  }
  if (preferred_sheet %in% sheets) {
    return(readxl::read_excel(file, sheet = preferred_sheet))
  }
  # Some historical workbooks store one worksheet under a generic title.
  if (length(sheets) == 1L) {
    return(readxl::read_excel(file, sheet = 1))
  }
  stop(paste0("Sheet '", preferred_sheet, "' was not found in ", file,
              ". Available sheets: ", paste(sheets, collapse = ", ")))
}

parse_number <- function(x) {
  if (is.numeric(x)) return(as.numeric(x))
  chr <- str_squish(as.character(x))
  chr <- gsub("\\s+", "", chr)
  # European/BR thousands separators are accepted alongside numeric cells.
  chr <- ifelse(grepl("^[0-9]{1,3}(\\.[0-9]{3})+(,[0-9]+)?$", chr),
                gsub(",", ".", gsub("\\.", "", chr)), chr)
  suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gsub(",", ".", chr, fixed = TRUE)))
}

parse_yes_no <- function(x, field_name) {
  if (is.logical(x)) return(ifelse(is.na(x), NA_character_, ifelse(x, "Yes", "No")))
  cleaned <- normalized_header(x)
  result <- dplyr::case_when(
    cleaned %in% c("sim", "yes", "true", "1", "y") ~ "Yes",
    cleaned %in% c("nao", "no", "false", "0", "n") ~ "No",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
  if (anyNA(result)) {
    stop(paste0("Unrecognized Yes/No values in ", field_name, ": ",
                paste(unique(as.character(x)[is.na(result)]), collapse = ", ")))
  }
  result
}

srq_palette <- c(
  "SRQ1" = "#D6EAF8", "SRQ2" = "#A9CCE3",
  "SRQ3" = "#5DADE2", "SRQ4" = "#2874A6", "SRQ5" = "#123B63"
)
```


# A.3 Data Synthesis — Results and Analysis of the Tertiary Study

```{r tertiary-study-data-setup, include=FALSE, fig.align="center"}
# Source for the authorship distribution and area-by-year chart.
tertiary_article_file <- project_file(
  "autores_classificados_refinado.xlsx", "article authorship and study areas"
)
tertiary_articles <- readxl::read_excel(tertiary_article_file)
dados <- tertiary_articles

# Sources for the corpus classification, selection, and network plots.
summary_file <- project_file("final_summary_table.xlsx", "qualified article summary")
qualified_summary <- readxl::read_excel(summary_file)
selection_file <- project_file("selection_process.xlsx", "selection funnel")
network_file <- project_file("term_normalization.xlsx", "term co-occurrence network")

tertiary_blue_palette <- c(
  "light" = "#D6EAF8", "light_medium" = "#A9CCE3",
  "medium" = "#5DADE2", "dark_medium" = "#2874A6",
  "dark" = "#123B63"
)

find_first_column <- function(data, candidates) {
  original <- names(data)
  hits <- which(normalized_header(original) %in% normalized_header(candidates))
  if (length(hits) == 0L) NA_character_ else original[hits[[1]]]
}

require_tertiary_articles <- function() {
  tertiary_articles
}

# Common article ID check (used to prevent inflation from repeated rows).
qualified_article_column <- project_columns(
  qualified_summary,
  c("article_id", "article", "id", "study_id", "study", "codigo", "article_code"),
  "qualified article ID in final_summary_table.xlsx"
)
```

```{r wordcloud-data-setup, include=FALSE, fig.align="center"}
prepare_wordcloud_words <- function(file_name) {
  data <- readxl::read_excel(project_file(file_name, "word-cloud source"))
  words <- unlist(data, use.names = FALSE)
  words <- as.character(words[!is.na(words)])
  words <- unlist(str_split(str_to_lower(words), "\\s+"))
  words <- str_replace_all(words, "[^a-z0-9-]", "")
  words[nchar(words) > 2 & !(words %in% c("and", "or", "with", "of", "in", "on"))]
}

save_wordcloud_once <- function(words, output_file) {
  frequencies <- sort(table(words), decreasing = TRUE)
  grDevices::png(output_file, width = 1800, height = 1400, res = 300)
  tryCatch({
    set.seed(123)
    wordcloud::wordcloud(
      words = names(frequencies), freq = as.numeric(frequencies),
      min.freq = 1, max.words = 200, random.order = FALSE,
      rot.per = 0.35, colors = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8, "Dark2")
    )
  }, finally = grDevices::dev.off())
  invisible(output_file)
}
```

## Figure A.11 — Distribution of authors by country

```{r distribution-authors-country, fig.width=9, fig.height=6, fig.align="center"}
# Count distinct authors, not one author per study-area row.
author_column <- project_columns(
  tertiary_articles,
  c("author", "authors", "autor", "autores", "Author", "Authors"),
  "author names in autores_classificados_refinado.xlsx"
)
country_column <- project_columns(
  tertiary_articles,
  c("country", "Country", "pais", "país"),
  "author countries in autores_classificados_refinado.xlsx"
)
author_country_data <- tertiary_articles %>%
  transmute(
    author_clean = str_squish(as.character(.data[[author_column]])),
    country_clean = str_squish(as.character(.data[[country_column]]))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(author_clean), author_clean != "",
         !is.na(country_clean), country_clean != "") %>%
  mutate(author_key = str_to_lower(author_clean)) %>%
  distinct(author_key, country_clean) %>%
  count(country_clean, name = "n_authors")
if (nrow(author_country_data) == 0L) {
  stop("No valid author/country records in autores_classificados_refinado.xlsx")
}

author_country_data <- author_country_data %>%
  arrange(n_authors, country_clean) %>%
  mutate(country_clean = factor(country_clean, levels = country_clean))

authors_country_plot <- ggplot(
  author_country_data,
  aes(
    x = n_authors,
    y = country_clean,
    fill = n_authors
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    width = 0.65
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = n_authors),
    hjust = -0.20,
    size = 3.6
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "lightblue",
    high = "navyblue"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(
      0,
      max(author_country_data$n_authors),
      by = 1
    ),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0.12)
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Authors by Country",
    x = "Number of Unique Authors",
    y = "Country"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 15,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 10
    ),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none"
  )


print(authors_country_plot)

ggsave(
  filename = "figure_authors_by_country.png",
  plot = authors_country_plot,
  width = 9,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
```

## Figure A.12 — Concentration of qualified articles by database

```{r qualified-articles-database, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, fig.align="center"}
database_column <- project_columns(
  qualified_summary,
  c("source", "database", "data_source", "publication_source", "base", "base_de_dados"),
  "publication database in final_summary_table.xlsx"
)
database_distribution <- qualified_summary %>%
  transmute(
    article_id = str_squish(as.character(.data[[qualified_article_column]])),
    database = str_squish(as.character(.data[[database_column]]))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(article_id), article_id != "",
         !is.na(database), database != "") %>%
  distinct(article_id, database) %>%
  mutate(
    database = dplyr::case_when(
      str_detect(str_to_lower(database), "ieee") ~ "IEEE Xplore",
      str_detect(str_to_lower(database), "sciencedirect|science direct|elsevier") ~ "ScienceDirect",
      str_detect(str_to_lower(database), "acm") ~ "ACM DL",
      str_detect(str_to_lower(database), "mdpi") ~ "MDPI",
      TRUE ~ database
    )
  ) %>%
  count(database, name = "n") %>%
  arrange(desc(n), database) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = n / sum(n),
    label = paste0(database, "\n", n, " (",
                   scales::percent(percentage, accuracy = 0.1), ")"),
    ymax = cumsum(n),
    ymin = lag(ymax, default = 0),
    label_position = (ymax + ymin) / 2
  )
if (nrow(database_distribution) == 0L) {
  stop("No qualified-article database records in final_summary_table.xlsx")
}

database_colors <- c(
  "IEEE Xplore" = "navyblue",
  "ScienceDirect" = "#3498DB",
  "ACM DL" = "lightblue",
  "MDPI" = "lightgrey"
)

qualified_database_plot <- ggplot(
  database_distribution,
  aes(
    x = 2,
    y = n,
    fill = database
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.9,
    width = 0.92
  ) +
  coord_polar(
    theta = "y"
  ) +
  xlim(
    0.55,
    2.75
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      y = label_position,
      x = 2.48,
      label = label
    ),
    size = 3.6,
    lineheight = 0.95
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = database_colors
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title = "Concentration of Qualified Articles by Database"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 15,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.margin = margin(
      20,
      25,
      20,
      25
    )
  )


print(qualified_database_plot)

ggsave(
  filename = "figure_qualified_articles_by_database.png",
  plot = qualified_database_plot,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
```

## Figure A.13 — Selection process retention across review stages

```{r selection-process-retention, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, fig.align="center"}
# Original R-specific sheet has three metadata rows before the headers.
selection_raw <- readxl::read_excel(
  selection_file, sheet = "R_Funnel_Input", skip = 3
)
stage_column <- project_columns(
  selection_raw,
  c("stage_short_label", "stage", "selection_stage", "phase", "etapa"),
  "stage label in selection_process.xlsx / R_Funnel_Input"
)
records_column <- project_columns(
  selection_raw,
  c("n_records", "records", "count", "n", "studies", "remaining", "retained"),
  "stage record count in selection_process.xlsx / R_Funnel_Input"
)
stage_order <- c("Retrieved", "Deduplicated", "Eligible", "Qualified")
selection_retention_data <- selection_raw %>%
  transmute(
    raw_stage = str_squish(as.character(.data[[stage_column]])),
    records = parse_number(.data[[records_column]])
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    stage_key = normalized_header(raw_stage),
    stage = case_when(
      str_detect(stage_key, "dedup|duplicat|unique|unico") ~ "Deduplicated",
      str_detect(stage_key, "qualif|includ|final|approve|accept") ~ "Qualified",
      str_detect(stage_key, "eligib|screen|select|criter|triagem") ~ "Eligible",
      str_detect(stage_key, "retriev|search|identif|import|recuper|initial|inicial") ~ "Retrieved",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(stage)) %>%
  mutate(stage = factor(stage, levels = stage_order)) %>%
  arrange(stage)
if (anyNA(selection_retention_data$records) ||
    nrow(selection_retention_data) != length(stage_order) ||
    anyDuplicated(selection_retention_data$stage)) {
  stop(paste0("R_Funnel_Input must provide a single valid n_records for ",
              paste(stage_order, collapse = ", "), ". ",
              "Check the sheet's stage_short_label and n_records columns."))
}
selection_retention_data <- selection_retention_data %>%
  mutate(
    retained = records / first(records),
    point_label = paste0(
      scales::comma(records, accuracy = 1), "\n(",
      scales::percent(retained, accuracy = 0.01), " of retrieved)"
    )
  )
selection_transition_data <- tibble::tibble(
  x = seq_len(nrow(selection_retention_data) - 1L) + 0.5,
  y = c(mean(selection_retention_data$retained[1:2]),
        mean(selection_retention_data$retained[2:3]), 0.010),
  removed = abs(diff(selection_retention_data$records))
) %>% mutate(label = scales::comma(removed, accuracy = 1))

selection_retention_plot <- ggplot(
  selection_retention_data,
  aes(
    x = stage,
    y = retained,
    group = 1
  )
) +
  geom_line(
    color = "#6FA8DC",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(size = records),
    shape = 21,
    fill = "navyblue",
    color = "navyblue",
    stroke = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_label(
    aes(
      label = point_label
    ),
    nudge_y = 0.075,
    size = 3.3,
    fill = "white",
    color = "grey20",
    label.size = 0.25
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = selection_transition_data,
    aes(
      x = x,
      y = y,
      label = label
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3.2,
    color = "grey35"
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(
    range = c(
      3,
      10
    ),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(
      0,
      1.12
    ),
    breaks = seq(
      0,
      1,
      by = 0.1
    ),
    labels = scales::percent_format(
      accuracy = 1
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Selection Process Retention Across Review Stages",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Point size represents the number of records; labels show ",
      "absolute counts and retention from the initial retrieval"
    ),
    x = "Selection Stage",
    y = "Records Retained (% of Retrieved)"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 15,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 9.5,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 10
    ),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


print(selection_retention_plot)

ggsave(
  filename = "figure_selection_process_retention.png",
  plot = selection_retention_plot,
  width = 10,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
```

## Figure A.14 — Quality score by qualified article

```{r quality-score-qualified-article, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.8, fig.align="center"}
quality_column <- project_columns(
  qualified_summary,
  c("quality_score", "quality score", "score", "final_score", "qa_score",
    "pontuacao", "pontuacao_final", "total_score", "quality_assessment_score"),
  "quality score in final_summary_table.xlsx"
)
quality_score_data <- qualified_summary %>%
  transmute(
    article_id = str_squish(as.character(.data[[qualified_article_column]])),
    quality_score = parse_number(.data[[quality_column]])
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(article_id), article_id != "") %>%
  distinct(article_id, quality_score) %>%
  arrange(article_id) %>%
  mutate(article_id = factor(article_id, levels = unique(article_id)))
if (anyNA(quality_score_data$quality_score) ||
    anyDuplicated(quality_score_data$article_id) || nrow(quality_score_data) == 0L) {
  stop("Invalid/duplicated quality scores in final_summary_table.xlsx")
}
mean_quality_score <- mean(quality_score_data$quality_score)

quality_score_plot <- ggplot(
  quality_score_data,
  aes(
    x = article_id,
    y = quality_score,
    fill = quality_score
  )
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = mean_quality_score,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "grey55",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_point(
    shape = 21,
    size = 5.5,
    color = "navyblue",
    stroke = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = ifelse(
        quality_score %% 1 == 0,
        as.character(
          as.integer(
            quality_score
          )
        ),
        format(
          quality_score,
          nsmall = 1,
          trim = TRUE
        )
      )
    ),
    nudge_y = 0.18,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "lightblue",
    high = "navyblue",
    limits = c(
      3.5,
      5
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(
      0,
      5.6
    ),
    breaks = seq(
      0,
      5,
      by = 0.5
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Quality Score by Qualified Article",
    subtitle = "Dashed line indicates the average quality score",
    x = "Qualified Article",
    y = "Quality Score"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 15,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 10,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 10
    ),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


print(quality_score_plot)

ggsave(
  filename = "figure_quality_score_by_article.png",
  plot = quality_score_plot,
  width = 9,
  height = 5.8,
  dpi = 300
)
```

## Figure A.16 — Article contribution across research questions

```{r heatmap-article-srq-contribution, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.5, fig.align="center"}
contribution_file <- project_file(
  c("article_srq_contribution.xlsx"),
  "article contribution (updated Tables 4.1–4.5)"
)
occurrence_detail <- readxl::read_excel(
  contribution_file, sheet = "Occurrence_Detail"
)
required <- c("article_id", "research_question")
if (!all(required %in% names(occurrence_detail))) {
  stop("Occurrence_Detail must contain article_id and research_question.")
}
# Do not silently plot the superseded matrix derived from old research-answer tables.
if ("source_table" %in% names(occurrence_detail)) {
  declared_tables <- unique(as.character(occurrence_detail$source_table))
  if (!all(paste0("Table 4.", 1:5) %in% declared_tables)) {
    stop(paste0(
      "article_srq_contribution.xlsx appears outdated. Update Occurrence_Detail ",
      "using Tables 4.1–4.5 before compiling A.16. Found: ",
      paste(declared_tables, collapse = ", ")
    ))
  }
}
if (anyNA(occurrence_detail$article_id) || anyNA(occurrence_detail$research_question)) {
  stop("Occurrence_Detail has incomplete article/SRQ identifiers.")
}
srq_contribution_data <- occurrence_detail %>%
  transmute(
    article_id = str_squish(as.character(article_id)),
    research_question = str_extract(
      str_to_upper(as.character(research_question)), "SRQ[1-5]"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(research_question), str_detect(article_id, "^A[0-9]+$")) %>%
  count(article_id, research_question, name = "occurrences") %>%
  complete(
    article_id = unique(article_id),
    research_question = paste0("SRQ", seq_len(5)),
    fill = list(occurrences = 0L)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    article_id = factor(article_id, levels = rev(sort(unique(article_id)))),
    research_question = factor(
      research_question,
      levels = paste0("SRQ", seq_len(5)),
      labels = c(
        "SRQ1 - Practices", "SRQ2 - Tools", "SRQ3 - Metrics",
        "SRQ4 - Challenges", "SRQ5 - Gaps and opportunities"
      )
    )
  )

srq_heatmap <- ggplot(
  srq_contribution_data,
  aes(x = research_question, y = article_id, fill = occurrences)
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = occurrences,
      color = occurrences >= max(srq_contribution_data$occurrences) / 2
    ),
    size = 3.5, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "lightblue", high = "navyblue", name = "Occurrences") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey20", "TRUE" = "white"), guide = "none") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Article Contribution Across Research Questions",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Cell values represent the number of contributions ",
      "identified for each article–SRQ combination"
    ),
    x = "Research Question", y = "Qualified Article"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 15, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, angle = 20, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom"
  )
print(srq_heatmap)
ggsave(
  filename = "figure_article_srq_contribution_heatmap.png",
  plot = srq_heatmap, width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 300
)
```

## Figure A.19 — Frequent and theme-related terms in keywords and search strings

```{r frequent-theme-related-terms, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, fig.align="center"}
# Frequencies are computed from the same two workbooks used by the word clouds.
# This avoids the previously hard-coded article-term frequency table.
term_frequency_tokens <- bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(token = keywords_words, source = "Keywords"),
  tibble::tibble(token = search_string_words, source = "Search strings")
) %>%
  mutate(token = str_to_lower(token))

# Keep the original cell text for counting multiword expressions as one term.
raw_keywords <- as.character(unlist(
  readxl::read_excel(project_file("keywords.xlsx", "keyword terms")),
  use.names = FALSE
))
raw_search_strings <- as.character(unlist(
  readxl::read_excel(project_file("search_string.xlsx", "search strings")),
  use.names = FALSE
))
raw_keywords <- tolower(raw_keywords[!is.na(raw_keywords)])
raw_search_strings <- tolower(raw_search_strings[!is.na(raw_search_strings)])

count_term_in_source <- function(word, source_name) {
  lower_word <- tolower(word)
  if (grepl(" ", lower_word, fixed = TRUE)) {
    raw_cells <- if (source_name == "Keywords") {
      raw_keywords
    } else {
      raw_search_strings
    }
    return(sum(stringr::str_count(raw_cells, stringr::fixed(lower_word))))
  }
  sum(term_frequency_tokens$source == source_name &
      term_frequency_tokens$token == lower_word)
}

term_order <- c(
  "devops",
  "continuous",
  "software",
  "security",
  "DevSecOps",
  "secdevops",
  "development",
  "engineering",
  "data",
  "systematic",
  "secure",
  "review",
  "literature",
  "compliance",
  "safety",
  "requirements",
  "privacy",
  "non-functional requirements",
  "NFR",
  "integrity",
  "confidentiality",
  "availability"
)


term_frequency_data <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  term = term_order,
  source = c("Keywords", "Search strings")
) %>%
  mutate(
    frequency = mapply(count_term_in_source, term, source),
    term = factor(term, levels = rev(term_order)),
    source = factor(source, levels = c("Keywords", "Search strings"))
  ) %>%
  filter(frequency > 0L)

frequent_terms_plot <- ggplot(
  term_frequency_data,
  aes(
    x = frequency,
    y = term,
    fill = source
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    position = position_dodge(
      width = 0.78
    ),
    width = 0.72
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = frequency
    ),
    position = position_dodge(
      width = 0.78
    ),
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Keywords" = "lightblue",
      "Search strings" = "navyblue"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 5),
    limits = c(0, max(term_frequency_data$frequency) * 1.12),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0)
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Frequent and Theme-Related Terms in Keywords and Search Strings",
    x = "Frequency",
    y = "Term",
    fill = "Source"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 15,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 9.5
    ),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )


print(frequent_terms_plot)

ggsave(
  filename = "figure_frequent_theme_related_terms.png",
  plot = frequent_terms_plot,
  width = 10,
  height = 8,
  dpi = 300
)
```

## Figure A.21 — Term co-occurrence network

```{r term-cooccurrence-network, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, fig.align="center"}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Importar os dados normalizados de coocorrência
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

# A primeira linha contém apenas o título da tabela.
# Os cabeçalhos reais estão na segunda linha.

cooccurrence_raw <- readxl::read_excel(
  path = network_file,
  sheet = "Cooccurrence_Edges",
  skip = 1,
  .name_repair = "unique"
)

# Identificar as colunas utilizando os cabeçalhos reais

term_a_column <- project_columns(
  cooccurrence_raw,
  c("term_a", "from", "source", "term_1", "term1"),
  "first term in term_normalization.xlsx / Cooccurrence_Edges"
)

term_b_column <- project_columns(
  cooccurrence_raw,
  c("term_b", "to", "target", "term_2", "term2"),
  "second term in term_normalization.xlsx / Cooccurrence_Edges"
)

occurrence_column <- project_columns(
  cooccurrence_raw,
  c(
    "cooccurrence_count",
    "co_occurrence_count",
    "cooccurrence",
    "weight",
    "n",
    "count"
  ),
  "co-occurrence counts in term_normalization.xlsx"
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Preparar e validar as relações entre os termos
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

term_edges <- cooccurrence_raw %>%
  transmute(
    from = stringr::str_squish(
      as.character(.data[[term_a_column]])
    ),

    to = stringr::str_squish(
      as.character(.data[[term_b_column]])
    ),

    cooccurrence = parse_number(
      .data[[occurrence_column]]
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(from),
    from != "",
    !is.na(to),
    to != "",
    from != to
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    from_ordered = pmin(from, to),
    to_ordered = pmax(from, to)
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    from = from_ordered,
    to = to_ordered
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    cooccurrence = sum(cooccurrence),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Validar a presença de relações e frequências válidas

if (
  nrow(term_edges) == 0L ||
  anyNA(term_edges$cooccurrence) ||
  any(term_edges$cooccurrence <= 0)
) {
  stop(
    "Cooccurrence_Edges contains no valid weighted term relationships."
  )
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Construir os nós e a rede
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

term_nodes <- tibble::tibble(
  name = sort(
    unique(
      c(term_edges$from, term_edges$to)
    )
  )
)

term_graph <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(
  d = term_edges,
  directed = FALSE,
  vertices = term_nodes
)

# Calcular o grau ponderado dos termos

igraph::V(term_graph)$weighted_degree <- igraph::strength(
  term_graph,
  weights = igraph::E(term_graph)$cooccurrence
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Gerar a visualização da rede de coocorrência
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

set.seed(123)

term_network_plot <- ggraph::ggraph(
  term_graph,
  layout = "fr"
) +

  # Conexões entre os termos
  ggraph::geom_edge_link(
    aes(
      width = cooccurrence,
      alpha = cooccurrence
    ),
    color = "grey65",
    show.legend = TRUE
  ) +

  # Nós da rede
  ggraph::geom_node_point(
    aes(
      size = weighted_degree,
      fill = weighted_degree
    ),
    shape = 21,
    color = "white",
    stroke = 0.6
  ) +

  # Identificação dos termos
  ggraph::geom_node_label(
    aes(
      label = name
    ),
    size = 2.8,
    label.size = 0.15,
    fill = scales::alpha(
      "white",
      0.90
    ),
    color = "grey20",
    repel = TRUE,
    max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +

  # Escala de cores dos nós
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#9FA8DA",
    high = "#3F51B5",
    name = "Weighted degree"
  ) +

  # Tamanho dos nós conforme grau ponderado
  scale_size_continuous(
    range = c(2, 7),
    breaks = c(10, 20, 30),
    name = "Weighted degree"
  ) +

  # Espessura das conexões
  ggraph::scale_edge_width_continuous(
    range = c(0.2, 1.2),
    breaks = 1:5,
    name = "Co-occurrence"
  ) +

  # Transparência das conexões
  ggraph::scale_edge_alpha_continuous(
    range = c(0.15, 0.55),
    guide = "none"
  ) +

  theme_void() +

  labs(
    title = "Term Co-occurrence Network",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Edges represent terms appearing together ",
      "in the same qualified article"
    )
  ) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 15,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 9.5,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),

    legend.position = "bottom",

    plot.margin = margin(
      15,
      25,
      15,
      25
    )
  ) +

  guides(
    size = guide_legend(
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0.5,
      order = 1
    ),

    fill = "none",

    edge_width = guide_legend(
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0.5,
      order = 2
    )
  )

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Apresentar e exportar o gráfico
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

print(term_network_plot)

ggsave(
  filename = "figure_term_cooccurrence_network.png",
  plot = term_network_plot,
  width = 11,
  height = 8,
  dpi = 300
)
```

```{r interviewee-data-setup, include=FALSE, fig.align="center"}
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)

# Carregar a planilha de caracterização dos entrevistados
interviewee_file <- project_file(

  "interview characterization"
)
interviewees_raw <- readxl::read_excel(interviewee_file)

# Verificar se todas as colunas necessárias estão disponíveis
required_interviewee_cols <- c(
  "ID",
  "Cargo atual",
  "Nível de senioridade",
  "Papel no pipeline CI/CD",
  "Nível de envolvimento com automação",
  "Setor da Empresa",
  "Grau de envolvimento do entrevistado com requisitos de privacidade",
  "O entrevistado já trabalhou com alguma regulamentação de privacidade?",
  "O entrevistado participa da verificação/testes de privacidade?",
  "O entrevistado participa da definição de requisitos de privacidade?",
  "A empresa possui práticas formais de DevOps?",
  "Existe política formal de privacidade na empresa?",
  "Privacidade é considerada no pipeline CI/CD?",
  "Nível de maturidade DevOps da Empresa (percepção do entrevistado)",
  "Sensibilidade dos dados tratados",
  "Tipo de dados",
  "Uso de automação de testes"
)

missing_interviewee_cols <- setdiff(
  required_interviewee_cols,

)

if (length(missing_interviewee_cols) > 0) {

    paste(
      "Colunas ausentes em caracterizacao_entrevistados.xlsx:",
      paste(missing_interviewee_cols, collapse = ", ")
    )
  )
}

# Renomear as colunas para facilitar seu uso nos gráficos

  transmute(

    participates_privacy_testing =

    participates_privacy_requirements =

    formal_devops =

    formal_privacy_policy =
      `Existe política formal de privacidade na empresa?`,
    privacy_in_pipeline =
      `Privacidade é considerada no pipeline CI/CD?`,
    devops_maturity =
      `Nível de maturidade DevOps da Empresa (percepção do entrevistado)`,
    data_sensitivity =

  ) %>%
  mutate(
```

```{r interviewee-professional-profile, fig.width=11, fig.height=6.5, fig.align="center"}
  arrange(category)

# Criar uma unidade visual para cada participante
pipeline_tiles <- pipeline_profile_data %>%
  tidyr::uncount(
    weights = n
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    tile_position = row_number(),
    x = ((tile_position - 1) %% 4) + 1,
    y = 4 - ((tile_position - 1) %/% 4),
    legend_label = factor(
      legend_label,
      levels = pipeline_profile_data$legend_label
    )
  )


# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Criar o painel de senioridade
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

seniority_colors <- stats::setNames(
  c("#D6EAF8", "#AED6F1", "#5DADE2", "#2874A6", "#123B63"),
  seniority_profile_data$legend_label
)

seniority_plot <- ggplot(
  seniority_tiles,
  aes(
    x = x,
    y = y,
    fill = legend_label
  )
) +
  geom_tile(
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 1.3,
    width = 0.92,
    height = 0.92
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = seniority_colors,
    drop = FALSE,
    name = "Seniority"
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:4,
    limits = c(0.5, 4.5)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = 1:4,
    limits = c(0.5, 4.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Seniority",
    subtitle = "Each square represents one participant",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 13,
      face = "bold",
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 9,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 10,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9)
  ) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(
      ncol = 2,
      byrow = TRUE,
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0.5
    )
  )

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Criar o painel de funções no pipeline CI/CD
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

pipeline_colors <- stats::setNames(
  c("#D6EAF8", "#85C1E9", "#2E86C1", "#123B63"),
  pipeline_profile_data$legend_label
)

pipeline_plot <- ggplot(
  pipeline_tiles,
  aes(
    x = x,
    y = y,
    fill = legend_label
  )
) +
  geom_tile(
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 1.3,
    width = 0.92,
    height = 0.92
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = pipeline_colors,
    drop = FALSE,
    name = "CI/CD Pipeline Role"
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:4,
    limits = c(0.5, 4.5)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = 1:4,
    limits = c(0.5, 4.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "CI/CD Pipeline Role",
    subtitle = "Each square represents one participant",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 13,
      face = "bold",
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 9,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 10,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9)
  ) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(
      ncol = 2,
      byrow = TRUE,
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0.5
    )
  )

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Combinar os dois painéis
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

professional_profile_plot <- (
  seniority_plot |
    pipeline_plot
) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "Professional Profile of Interview Participants",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        size = 15,
        hjust = 0.5,
        face = "bold"
      )
    )
  )


print(professional_profile_plot)

ggsave(
  filename = "figure_interviewee_professional_profile.png",
  plot = professional_profile_plot,
  width = 11,
  height = 6.5,
  dpi = 300
)
```

## Figure B.12 — Distribution of interviewees by company sector

```{r interviewee-company-sectors, fig.width=10.5, fig.height=7, fig.align="center"}
# Preparar a distribuição dos participantes por setor
company_sector_data <- interviewees %>%
  count(
    company_sector_en,
    name = "n"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = n / sum(n),

    sector_label = stringr::str_wrap(
      company_sector_en,
      width = 43
    ),

    representation_group = if_else(
      n > 1,
      "Multiple participants",
      "One participant"
    ),

    value_label = paste0(
      n,
      " (",
      scales::percent(
        percentage,
        accuracy = 0.1
      ),
      ")"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    n,
    company_sector_en
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # A ordem crescente dos níveis posiciona
    # os maiores valores no topo do gráfico
    sector_label = factor(
      sector_label,
      levels = sector_label
    ),

    representation_group = factor(
      representation_group,
      levels = c(
        "One participant",
        "Multiple participants"
      )
    )
  )


# Gerar o gráfico horizontal ordenado

  company_sector_data,
```

## Figure B.13 — Privacy governance and operational participation

```{r privacy-governance-overview, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, fig.align="center"}
privacy_governance_data <- interviewees %>%
  select(
    privacy_regulation_experience_en,
    participates_privacy_testing_en,
    participates_privacy_requirements_en,
    formal_devops_en,
    formal_privacy_policy_en,
    privacy_in_pipeline_en
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "indicator",
    values_to = "response"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    indicator = recode(
      indicator,
      "privacy_regulation_experience_en" =
        "Previous experience with privacy regulation",
      "participates_privacy_testing_en" =
        "Participation in privacy testing",
      "participates_privacy_requirements_en" =
        "Participation in privacy requirements definition",
      "formal_devops_en" =
        "Formal DevOps practices",
      "formal_privacy_policy_en" =
        "Formal privacy policy",
      "privacy_in_pipeline_en" =
        "Privacy considered in the CI/CD pipeline"
    )
  ) %>%
  count(
    indicator,
    response,
    name = "n"
  ) %>%
  group_by(indicator) %>%
  complete(
    response = c("Yes", "No"),
    fill = list(n = 0)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    total = sum(n),
    percentage = n / total,
    signed_percentage = ifelse(
      response == "Yes",
      percentage,
      -percentage
    ),
    label = ifelse(
      n > 0,
      paste0(
        n,
        " (",
        scales::percent(
          percentage,
          accuracy = 1
        ),
        ")"
      ),
      ""
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    indicator = factor(
      indicator,
      levels = rev(c(
        "Previous experience with privacy regulation",
        "Participation in privacy testing",
        "Participation in privacy requirements definition",
        "Formal DevOps practices",
        "Formal privacy policy",
        "Privacy considered in the CI/CD pipeline"
      ))
    ),
    response = factor(
      response,
      levels = c("No", "Yes")
    )
  )


privacy_governance_plot <- ggplot(
  privacy_governance_data,
  aes(
    x = signed_percentage,
    y = indicator,
    fill = response
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    width = 0.65
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    color = "grey40",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = privacy_governance_data %>%
      filter(n > 0),
    aes(
      label = label,
      hjust = ifelse(
        signed_percentage > 0,
        -0.1,
        1.1
      )
    ),
    size = 3.2
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Yes" = "navyblue",
      "No" = "lightblue"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(-1.18, 1.18),
    breaks = seq(-1, 1, by = 0.25),
    labels = function(x) {
      scales::percent(
        abs(x),
        accuracy = 1
      )
    }
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Privacy Governance and Operational Participation",
    x = "Percentage of Participants",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Response"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 15,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )


print(privacy_governance_plot)

ggsave(
  filename = "figure_privacy_governance_overview.png",
  plot = privacy_governance_plot,
  width = 10,
  height = 6.5,
  dpi = 300
)
```

## Figure B.14 — Privacy activities by CI/CD pipeline role

```{r pipeline-role-privacy-activities, fig.width=12, fig.height=6.2, fig.align="center"}
# Preparar as taxas de participação por papel no pipeline
pipeline_privacy_activity_data <- interviewees %>%
  select(
    pipeline_role_en,
    participates_privacy_testing_en,
    participates_privacy_requirements_en
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      participates_privacy_requirements_en,
      participates_privacy_testing_en
    ),
    names_to = "activity",
    values_to = "response"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    activity = recode(
      activity,
      "participates_privacy_requirements_en" =
        "Privacy requirements definition",
      "participates_privacy_testing_en" =
        "Privacy verification/testing"
    ),

    activity = factor(
      activity,
      levels = c(
        "Privacy requirements definition",
        "Privacy verification/testing"
      )
    ),

    pipeline_role_en = factor(
      pipeline_role_en,
      levels = c(
        "Release/Deploy",
        "Quality",
        "Development",
        "Monitoring"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    activity,
    pipeline_role_en
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    group_size = n(),
    participants_yes = sum(
      response == "Yes"
    ),
    participation_rate =
      participants_yes / group_size,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    role_position = as.numeric(
      pipeline_role_en
    ),

    value_label = paste0(
      participants_yes,
      "/",
      group_size,
      "\n",
      scales::percent(
        participation_rate,
        accuracy = 1
      )
    ),

    label_position = case_when(
      participation_rate == 0 ~ 0.11,
      participation_rate >= 0.9 ~ 1.03,
      TRUE ~ participation_rate + 0.09
    )
  )


pipeline_role_labels <- c(
  "Release/\nDeploy",
  "Quality",
  "Development",
  "Monitoring"
)

pipeline_privacy_activity_plot <- ggplot(
  pipeline_privacy_activity_data,
  aes(
    x = role_position,
    y = participation_rate,
    group = activity
  )
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = seq(
      0.25,
      1,
      by = 0.25
    ),
    color = "grey82",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 1:4,
    color = "grey88",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_polygon(
    aes(
      fill = activity,
      color = activity
    ),
    alpha = 0.28,
    linewidth = 1.2,
    linejoin = "round",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(
      fill = activity
    ),
    shape = 21,
    size = 5,
    color = "white",
    stroke = 0.9,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      y = label_position,
      label = value_label
    ),
    size = 3.2,
    lineheight = 0.9,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "grey20"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ activity,
    ncol = 2
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Privacy requirements definition" =
        "lightblue",
      "Privacy verification/testing" =
        "navyblue"
    )
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Privacy requirements definition" =
        "steelblue",
      "Privacy verification/testing" =
        "navyblue"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:4,
    labels = pipeline_role_labels,
    limits = c(
      0.5,
      4.5
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(
      0,
      1.1
    ),
    breaks = seq(
      0.25,
      1,
      by = 0.25
    ),
    labels = scales::percent_format(
      accuracy = 1
    ),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0)
    )
  ) +
  coord_polar(
    start = -pi / 4,
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Privacy Activities by CI/CD Pipeline Role",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Distance from the center represents the participation rate; ",
      "labels show participants and percentages"
    ),
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 15,
      hjust = 0.5,
      face = "bold"
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 10,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),

    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 10.5,
      face = "bold"
    ),

    axis.text.x = element_text(
      size = 9.5,
      face = "bold",
      color = "grey20"
    ),

    axis.text.y = element_text(
      size = 8,
      color = "grey40"
    ),

    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none",

    # Separar os rótulos Quality e Monitoring
    # localizados entre os dois painéis
    panel.spacing.x = grid::unit(
      3,
      "cm"
    ),

    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 10,
      r = 25,
      b = 10,
      l = 25
    )
  )


print(pipeline_privacy_activity_plot)

ggsave(
  filename = "figure_pipeline_role_privacy_activities.png",
  plot = pipeline_privacy_activity_plot,
  width = 12,
  height = 6.2,
  dpi = 300
)
```

```{r thematic-analysis-data-setup, include=FALSE, fig.align="center"}
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(forcats)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(ggrepel)

theme_file <- project_file(
  c("code_book_temas_revisados.xlsx"),
  "final thematic codebook"
)

if (!file.exists(theme_file)) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "The file '",
      theme_file,
      "' was not found in the project directory."
    )
  )
}

# Ler integralmente a planilha sem assumir que a primeira linha é o cabeçalho
theme_sheets <- readxl::excel_sheets(theme_file)
theme_sheet <- if ("Resumo dos temas" %in% theme_sheets) "Resumo dos temas" else theme_sheets[[1]]
raw_theme_sheet <- readxl::read_excel(
  path = theme_file,
  sheet = theme_sheet,
  col_names = FALSE
)

names(raw_theme_sheet) <- paste0(
  "V",
  seq_along(raw_theme_sheet)
)

required_columns <- paste0("V", 1:9)

missing_columns <- setdiff(
  required_columns,
  names(raw_theme_sheet)
)

if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "The spreadsheet does not contain the expected nine columns. ",
      "Missing columns: ",
      paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")
    )
  )
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Temas finais
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

theme_data <- raw_theme_sheet %>%
  transmute(
    group = as.character(V1),
    theme_id = as.character(V2),
    theme = as.character(V3),
    description = as.character(V4),
    codes = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(V5)
    ),
    percentage = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(V6)
    ),
    clusters = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(V7)
    ),
    incorporated_clusters = as.character(V8),
    analytical_rationale = as.character(V9)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    stringr::str_detect(
      theme_id,
      "^SRQ[1-5]-T\\d{2}$"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    srq = stringr::str_extract(
      theme_id,
      "SRQ[1-5]"
    ),

    srq = factor(
      srq,
      levels = paste0(
        "SRQ",
        1:5
      )
    ),

    theme_order = as.integer(
      stringr::str_extract(
        theme_id,
        "\\d{2}$"
      )
    ),

    theme_code = stringr::str_extract(
      theme_id,
      "T\\d{2}$"
    ),

    theme_name_wrapped = stringr::str_wrap(
      theme,
      width = 34
    ),

    theme_full_label = paste0(
      theme_id,
      " — ",
      theme_name_wrapped
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    srq,
    theme_order
  )

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Resumo quantitativo por grupo
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

summary_data <- raw_theme_sheet %>%
  transmute(
    group = as.character(V1),
    codes = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(V2)
    ),
    final_themes = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(V3)
    ),
    incorporated_clusters = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(V4)
    ),
    discarded_clusters = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(V5)
    ),
    codes_without_theme = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(V6)
    ),
    observation = as.character(V7)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    stringr::str_detect(
      group,
      "^([1-6] - |Total$)"
    )
  )

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Clusters descartados
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

discarded_cluster_data <- raw_theme_sheet %>%
  transmute(
    group = as.character(V1),
    cluster_id = as.character(V2),
    discarded_cluster = as.character(V3),
    codes = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(V4)
    ),
    analytical_rationale = as.character(V5)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    stringr::str_detect(
      cluster_id,
      "^SRQ[1-5]-C\\d{2}$"
    )
  )

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Validações estruturais
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

if (nrow(theme_data) == 0) {
  stop(
    "No final themes were identified in the spreadsheet."
  )
}

if (anyDuplicated(theme_data$theme_id) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Duplicated theme IDs were identified."
  )
}

if (
  any(
    is.na(theme_data$codes)
  ) ||
  any(
    is.na(theme_data$percentage)
  ) ||
  any(
    is.na(theme_data$clusters)
  )
) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "At least one theme contains missing or non-numeric ",
      "values in Codes, Percentage, or Number of Clusters."
    )
  )
}

# Paleta comum aos gráficos temáticos
srq_palette <- c(
  "SRQ1" = "#D6EAF8",
  "SRQ2" = "#A9CCE3",
  "SRQ3" = "#5DADE2",
  "SRQ4" = "#2874A6",
  "SRQ5" = "#123B63"
)

# Resumo utilizado para conferência
thematic_dataset_summary <- theme_data %>%
  group_by(srq) %>%
  summarise(
    themes = n(),
    codes_in_themes = sum(codes),
    incorporated_clusters = sum(clusters),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

theme_translations <- c(


  "SRQ1-T01" = "Data lifecycle control",
  "SRQ1-T02" = "Privacy beyond security",
  "SRQ1-T03" = "Privacy as a systemic responsibility",
  "SRQ1-T04" = "Context-dependent privacy",

  "SRQ2-T01" = "Data lifecycle controls",
  "SRQ2-T02" = "Governance and legitimacy of data processing",
  "SRQ2-T03" = "Demonstrable compliance through evidence",
  "SRQ2-T04" = "Capacity building for everyday practices",
  "SRQ2-T05" = "Identity and access governance",
  "SRQ2-T06" = "Layered technical protection",
  "SRQ2-T07" = "Secure and verifiable development",
  "SRQ2-T08" = "Adaptable formal processes",
  "SRQ2-T09" = "Security substituting for privacy",
  "SRQ2-T10" = "Uneven and reactive verification",

  "SRQ3-T01" = "Privacy by design",
  "SRQ3-T02" = "Automated verification in the pipeline",
  "SRQ3-T03" = "Pipeline and environment protection",
  "SRQ3-T04" = "Continuous post-deployment verification",
  "SRQ3-T05" = "Partially integrated privacy",

  "SRQ4-T01" = "Indirect functional verification",

  "SRQ4-T03" = "Immature direct privacy testing",
  "SRQ4-T04" = "Test data protection",
  "SRQ4-T05" = "Hybrid test execution",
  "SRQ4-T06" = "Governance of test findings",

  "SRQ5-T01" = "Insufficient culture and competencies",
  "SRQ5-T02" = "Fragmented and informal governance",
  "SRQ5-T03" = "Privacy deprioritized by business priorities",
  "SRQ5-T04" = "Incomplete technical coverage",

)
```

```{r themes-overview-by-srq, fig.width=12, fig.height=4, fig.align="center"}
thematic_structure_data <- theme_data %>%
  group_by(srq) %>%
  mutate(
    number_of_themes = n(),

    panel_label = paste0(
      srq,

      number_of_themes,
      ")"
    ),

    label_color = if_else(
      srq %in% c(
        "SRQ1",
        "SRQ2"
      ),
      "navyblue",
      "white"
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

panel_levels <- thematic_structure_data %>%
  distinct(
    srq,
    panel_label
  ) %>%
  arrange(srq) %>%
  pull(panel_label)

thematic_structure_data <- thematic_structure_data %>%
  mutate(
    panel_label = factor(
      panel_label,
      levels = panel_levels
    )
  )


themes_overview_plot <- ggplot(
```

## Figure B.18 — Traceability of the thematic consolidation process

```{r thematic-consolidation-traceability, fig.width=12, fig.height=8, fig.align="center"}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Identificar exclusivamente as linhas do resumo quantitativo
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

# summary_data foi criado no chunk de preparação dos temas.
# A aba contém outras linhas com os mesmos identificadores SRQ.
# Por isso, selecionar somente os registros quantitativos completos.

summary_validated <- summary_data %>%
  mutate(
    group = stringr::str_squish(
      stringr::str_replace_all(
        as.character(group),
        "\u00A0",
        " "
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(codes),
    !is.na(final_themes),
    !is.na(incorporated_clusters),
    !is.na(discarded_clusters),
    !is.na(codes_without_theme)
  )

# Recuperar os cinco grupos SRQ
srq_summary_rows <- summary_validated %>%
  filter(
    stringr::str_detect(
      group,
      "^[1-5]\\s*-\\s*SRQ[1-5]$"
    )
  )

# Recuperar o grupo Outros achados
other_summary_row <- summary_validated %>%
  filter(
    stringr::str_detect(
      group,
      "^6\\s*-\\s*"
    )
  )

# Recuperar a linha de totais
total_summary_row <- summary_validated %>%
  filter(
    group == "Total"
  )

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Validar os registros recuperados
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

expected_srq_count <- length(
  levels(theme_data$srq)
)

if (
  nrow(srq_summary_rows) != expected_srq_count ||
  nrow(other_summary_row) != 1L ||
  nrow(total_summary_row) != 1L
) {
  print(
    summary_validated %>%
      select(
        group,
        codes,
        final_themes,
        incorporated_clusters,
        discarded_clusters,
        codes_without_theme
      )
  )

  stop(
    paste0(
      "Resumo dos temas: expected ",
      expected_srq_count,
      " SRQ rows, one Other findings row ",
      "and one Total row. Found: ",
      nrow(srq_summary_rows),
      ", ",
      nrow(other_summary_row),
      " and ",
      nrow(total_summary_row),
      ", respectively."
    )
  )
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Calcular as quantidades diretamente da planilha
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

# Total de códigos iniciais
total_codes <- total_summary_row$codes[[1]]

# Códigos inicialmente associados às cinco SRQs
codes_assigned_to_srqs <- sum(
  srq_summary_rows$codes
)

# Códigos classificados como Outros achados
other_findings_codes <- other_summary_row$codes[[1]]

# Códigos efetivamente incorporados aos temas finais
codes_in_final_themes <- sum(
  theme_data$codes
)

# Clusters incorporados aos temas
incorporated_clusters_total <- sum(
  theme_data$clusters
)

# Clusters descartados durante a consolidação
discarded_clusters_total <- sum(
  srq_summary_rows$discarded_clusters
)

# Códigos pertencentes aos clusters descartados
codes_in_discarded_clusters <- sum(
  srq_summary_rows$codes_without_theme
)

# Total de clusters provisórios
provisional_clusters_total <-
  incorporated_clusters_total +
  discarded_clusters_total

# Número de temas finais
final_themes_total <- dplyr::n_distinct(
  theme_data$theme_id
)

# Códigos que não integram os temas finais
codes_without_final_theme <-
  other_findings_codes +
  codes_in_discarded_clusters

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Validar a consistência quantitativa
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

traceability_counts <- c(
  total_codes = total_codes,
  codes_assigned_to_srqs = codes_assigned_to_srqs,
  other_findings_codes = other_findings_codes,
  codes_in_final_themes = codes_in_final_themes,
  incorporated_clusters_total = incorporated_clusters_total,
  discarded_clusters_total = discarded_clusters_total,
  codes_in_discarded_clusters = codes_in_discarded_clusters,
  provisional_clusters_total = provisional_clusters_total,
  final_themes_total = final_themes_total,
  codes_without_final_theme = codes_without_final_theme
)

# Verificar valores ausentes, inválidos ou negativos
if (
  anyNA(traceability_counts) ||
  any(!is.finite(traceability_counts)) ||
  any(traceability_counts < 0)
) {
  stop(
    "Invalid or missing values in thematic traceability counts."
  )
}

# Verificar a distribuição dos códigos iniciais
if (
  codes_assigned_to_srqs +
    other_findings_codes != total_codes
) {
  stop(
    "Initial code distribution does not match the total."
  )
}

# Verificar a consolidação dos códigos das SRQs
if (
  codes_in_final_themes +
    codes_in_discarded_clusters !=
    codes_assigned_to_srqs
) {
  stop(
    "Incorporated and discarded codes do not match the SRQ total."
  )
}

# Verificar os códigos sem tema final
if (
  codes_in_final_themes +
    codes_without_final_theme != total_codes
) {
  stop(
    "Codes in final themes and codes without a theme do not reconcile."
  )
}

# Comparar clusters e temas com a linha Total da planilha
if (
  incorporated_clusters_total !=
    total_summary_row$incorporated_clusters[[1]] ||
  discarded_clusters_total !=
    total_summary_row$discarded_clusters[[1]] ||
  final_themes_total !=
    total_summary_row$final_themes[[1]] ||
  codes_without_final_theme !=
    total_summary_row$codes_without_theme[[1]]
) {
  stop(
    "Thematic traceability totals do not reconcile with the source table."
  )
}

# Conferência dos valores calculados
print(
  tibble::tibble(
    Metric = names(traceability_counts),
    Value = as.numeric(traceability_counts)
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Formatar as quantidades para apresentação
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

format_count <- function(value) {
  scales::comma(
    value,
    accuracy = 1,
    big.mark = ",",
    decimal.mark = "."
  )
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Construir os nós do fluxograma
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

flow_nodes <- tibble::tibble(
  node_id = c(
    "initial_codes",
    "srq_codes",
    "other_findings",
    "incorporated",
    "discarded",
    "final_themes",
    "without_theme"
  ),

  x = c(
    0.50,
    0.25,
    0.75,
    0.18,
    0.50,
    0.18,
    0.75
  ),

  y = c(
    5.55,
    4.15,
    4.15,
    2.75,
    2.75,
    1.15,
    1.15
  ),

  node_width = c(
    0.34,
    0.36,
    0.34,
    0.31,
    0.28,
    0.29,
    0.37
  ),

  node_height = c(
    0.58,
    0.72,
    0.72,
    0.72,
    0.72,
    0.72,
    0.82
  ),

  stage = c(
    "Initial coding",
    "Thematic grouping",
    "Excluded grouping",
    "Incorporated clusters",
    "Discarded clusters",
    "Final themes",
    "Codes without final theme"
  ),

  text_color = c(
    "white",
    "white",
    "navyblue",
    "white",
    "navyblue",
    "white",
    "navyblue"
  ),

  label = c(
    paste0(
      format_count(total_codes),
      " initial codes"
    ),

    paste0(
      format_count(codes_assigned_to_srqs),
      " codes assigned to SRQ1–SRQ5\n",
      provisional_clusters_total,
      " provisional clusters"
    ),

    paste0(
      format_count(other_findings_codes),
      " codes classified as\n",
      "“Other findings”"
    ),

    paste0(
      format_count(codes_in_final_themes),
      " codes\n",
      incorporated_clusters_total,
      " incorporated clusters"
    ),

    paste0(
      format_count(codes_in_discarded_clusters),
      " codes\n",
      discarded_clusters_total,
      " discarded clusters"
    ),

    paste0(
      final_themes_total,
      " final themes"
    ),

    paste0(
      format_count(codes_without_final_theme),
      " codes without a final theme\n",
      format_count(other_findings_codes),
      " other findings + ",
      format_count(codes_in_discarded_clusters),
      " discarded"
    )
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    xmin = x - node_width / 2,
    xmax = x + node_width / 2,
    ymin = y - node_height / 2,
    ymax = y + node_height / 2
  )

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Construir as conexões entre os nós
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

flow_arrows <- tibble::tibble(
  arrow_id = c(
    "initial_to_srq",
    "initial_to_other",
    "srq_to_incorporated",
    "srq_to_discarded",
    "incorporated_to_themes",
    "discarded_to_without",
    "other_to_without"
  ),

  x = c(
    0.46,
    0.54,
    0.22,
    0.29,
    0.18,
    0.50,
    0.75
  ),

  y = c(
    5.25,
    5.25,
    3.79,
    3.79,
    2.39,
    2.39,
    3.79
  ),

  xend = c(
    0.25,
    0.75,
    0.18,
    0.50,
    0.18,
    0.75,
    0.75
  ),

  yend = c(
    4.52,
    4.52,
    3.12,
    3.12,
    1.51,
    1.56,
    1.56
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Gerar o gráfico de rastreabilidade
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

thematic_traceability_plot <- ggplot() +

  geom_curve(
    data = flow_arrows,
    aes(
      x = x,
      y = y,
      xend = xend,
      yend = yend
    ),
    curvature = 0.08,
    color = "grey55",
    linewidth = 0.9,
    arrow = grid::arrow(
      length = grid::unit(
        0.17,
        "inches"
      ),
      type = "closed"
    )
  ) +

  geom_rect(
    data = flow_nodes,
    aes(
      xmin = xmin,
      xmax = xmax,
      ymin = ymin,
      ymax = ymax,
      fill = stage
    ),
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +

  geom_text(
    data = flow_nodes,
    aes(
      x = x,
      y = y,
      label = label,
      color = text_color
    ),
    size = 4,
    fontface = "bold",
    lineheight = 0.95
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Initial coding" = "#123B63",
      "Thematic grouping" = "#2874A6",
      "Excluded grouping" = "#D6EAF8",
      "Incorporated clusters" = "#2874A6",
      "Discarded clusters" = "#D6EAF8",
      "Final themes" = "#123B63",
      "Codes without final theme" = "#D6EAF8"
    )
  ) +

  scale_color_identity() +

  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(0, 1),
    ylim = c(0.55, 6),
    clip = "off"
  ) +

  theme_void() +

  labs(
    title = "Traceability of the Thematic Consolidation Process",

    subtitle = paste0(
      "Flow from the initial codes to the final themes ",
      "and analytically excluded material"
    ),

    caption = paste0(
      "Counts describe the consolidation process and do not represent ",
      "automatic measures of thematic relevance."
    )
  ) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 15,
      hjust = 0.5,
      face = "bold"
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 10,
      hjust = 0.5,
      margin = margin(b = 12)
    ),

    plot.caption = element_text(
      size = 9,
      hjust = 0.5,
      color = "grey35",
      margin = margin(t = 10)
    ),

    legend.position = "none",

    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 15,
      r = 30,
      b = 15,
      l = 30
    )
  )

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Apresentar e exportar
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

print(thematic_traceability_plot)

ggsave(
  filename = "figure_thematic_consolidation_traceability.png",
  plot = thematic_traceability_plot,
  width = 12,
  height = 8,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)
```

## Figure B.19 — Hierarchical map of research questions and final themes

```{r thematic-hierarchy-sunburst, fig.width=10, fig.height=10, fig.align="center"}
theme_sunburst_data <- theme_data %>%
  arrange(
    srq,
    theme_order
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    theme_end = cumsum(codes),

    theme_start = lag(
      theme_end,
      default = 0
    ),

    theme_mid = (
      theme_start +
        theme_end
    ) / 2
  )

total_theme_codes <- sum(
  theme_sunburst_data$codes
)

theme_sunburst_data <- theme_sunburst_data %>%
  mutate(
    raw_label_angle =
      90 -
      360 *
      theme_mid /
      total_theme_codes,

    label_hjust = if_else(
      raw_label_angle < -90,
      1,
      0
    ),

    label_angle = if_else(
      raw_label_angle < -90,
      raw_label_angle + 180,
      raw_label_angle
    )
  )

srq_sunburst_data <- theme_sunburst_data %>%
  group_by(srq) %>%
  summarise(
    codes = sum(codes),
    segment_start = min(theme_start),
    segment_end = max(theme_end),
    segment_mid = (
      segment_start +
        segment_end
    ) / 2,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    srq_label = paste0(
      srq,
      "\n",
      codes,
      " codes"
    ),

    text_color = if_else(
      srq %in% c(
        "SRQ1",
        "SRQ2"
      ),
      "navyblue",
      "white"
    )
  )


thematic_hierarchy_plot <- ggplot() +
  # Anel interno: perguntas de pesquisa
  geom_rect(
    data = srq_sunburst_data,
    aes(
      xmin = 0.75,
      xmax = 1.65,
      ymin = segment_start,
      ymax = segment_end,
      fill = srq
    ),
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +

  # Anel externo: temas finais
  geom_rect(
    data = theme_sunburst_data,
    aes(
      xmin = 1.65,
      xmax = 3,
      ymin = theme_start,
      ymax = theme_end,
      fill = srq
    ),
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.4,
    alpha = 0.75
  ) +

  # Rótulos das perguntas de pesquisa
  geom_text(
    data = srq_sunburst_data,
    aes(
      x = 1.20,
      y = segment_mid,
      label = srq_label,
      color = text_color
    ),
    size = 3.2,
    fontface = "bold",
    lineheight = 0.9
  ) +

  # IDs dos temas ao redor do anel externo
  geom_text(
    data = theme_sunburst_data,
    aes(
      x = 3.22,
      y = theme_mid,
      label = theme_code,
      angle = label_angle,
      hjust = label_hjust
    ),
    size = 2.7,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "grey20"
  ) +

  coord_polar(
    theta = "y",
    clip = "off"
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = srq_palette,
    name = "Research Question"
  ) +

  scale_color_identity() +

  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(
      0.3,
      3.75
    ),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0)
    )
  ) +

  theme_void() +

  labs(
    title = "Hierarchical Map of Research Questions and Final Themes",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "The inner ring represents SRQs; the outer ring represents themes; ",
      "segment size is proportional to the number of codes"
    )
  ) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 15,
      hjust = 0.5,
      face = "bold"
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 10,
      hjust = 0.5,
      margin = margin(
        b = 10
      )
    ),

    legend.position = "bottom",

    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 10,
      face = "bold"
    ),

    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 9
    ),

    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 15,
      r = 45,
      b = 15,
      l = 45
    )
  ) +

  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0.5
    )
  )


print(thematic_hierarchy_plot)

ggsave(
  filename = "figure_thematic_hierarchy_sunburst.png",
  plot = thematic_hierarchy_plot,
  width = 10,
  height = 10,
  dpi = 300
)
```

## Figure B.20 — Relationship between incorporated clusters and theme codes

```{r theme-codes-clusters-relationship, fig.width=11, fig.height=7.5, fig.align="center"}
theme_scatter_data <- theme_data %>%
  mutate(
    percentage_label = scales::percent(
      percentage,
      accuracy = 0.1
    )
  )


theme_codes_clusters_plot <- ggplot(
  theme_scatter_data,
  aes(
    x = clusters,
    y = codes
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    aes(
      fill = srq,
      size = percentage
    ),
    shape = 21,
    color = "grey25",
    stroke = 0.35,
    alpha = 0.60
  ) +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(
    aes(
      label = theme_id,
      color = srq
    ),
    size = 3,
    fontface = "bold",
    fill = scales::alpha(
      "white",
      0.88
    ),
    label.size = 0.18,
    box.padding = 0.45,
    point.padding = 0.30,
    label.padding = grid::unit(
      0.12,
      "lines"
    ),
    min.segment.length = 0,
    segment.color = "grey65",
    segment.alpha = 0.8,
    segment.linewidth = 0.35,
    max.overlaps = Inf,
    seed = 123,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = srq_palette,
    name = "Research Question"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = srq_palette
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(
    range = c(
      4,
      11
    ),
    labels = scales::percent_format(
      accuracy = 1
    ),
    name = "Share within SRQ"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(
      0,
      max(theme_scatter_data$clusters, na.rm = TRUE) + 1,
      by = 2
    ),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(
        0.05,
        0.12
      )
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(
      n = 7
    ),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(
        0.06,
        0.18
      )
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Relationship between Incorporated Clusters and Theme Codes",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Theme IDs identify individual themes; point size represents ",
      "the theme's share of codes within its SRQ"
    ),
    x = "Number of Incorporated Clusters",
    y = "Number of Codes"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 15,
      hjust = 0.5,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 10,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    axis.title = element_text(
      size = 10.5
    ),
    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 9.5
    ),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 10,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 9
    )
  ) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0.5,
      order = 1,
      override.aes = list(
        size = 4,
        alpha = 1
      )
    ),
    size = guide_legend(
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0.5,
      order = 2,
      override.aes = list(
        fill = "grey30",
        alpha = 0.85,
        color = "grey25"
      )
    ),
    color = "none"
  )


print(theme_codes_clusters_plot)

ggsave(
  filename = "figure_theme_codes_clusters_relationship.png",
  plot = theme_codes_clusters_plot,

)
```

## Figure B.21 — Relative distribution of themes within each research question

```{r theme-distribution-within-srq, fig.width=12, fig.height=14, fig.align="center"}
theme_distribution_data <- theme_data %>%
  mutate(theme_en = unname(theme_translations[theme_id]))

# Interromper a execução caso algum tema não tenha sido traduzido
untranslated_themes <- theme_distribution_data %>%
  filter(
    is.na(theme_en)
  ) %>%
  distinct(
    theme_id,
    theme
  )

if (nrow(untranslated_themes) > 0) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "The following themes do not have an English translation: ",
      paste(
        untranslated_themes$theme_id,
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  )
}

# Preparar a ordenação e os rótulos apresentados no gráfico
theme_distribution_data <- theme_distribution_data %>%
  arrange(
    srq,
    percentage
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    theme_key = paste0(
      as.character(srq),
      "__",
      theme_id
    ),

    theme_axis_label = paste0(
      theme_id,
      " — ",
      stringr::str_wrap(
        theme_en,
        width = 34
      )
    )
  )

theme_distribution_levels <-
  theme_distribution_data$theme_key

theme_distribution_labels <- stats::setNames(
  theme_distribution_data$theme_axis_label,
  theme_distribution_data$theme_key
)

theme_distribution_data <- theme_distribution_data %>%
  mutate(
    theme_key = factor(
      theme_key,
      levels = theme_distribution_levels
    )
  )

maximum_theme_percentage <- max(
  theme_distribution_data$percentage,
  na.rm = TRUE
)


theme_distribution_plot <- ggplot(
  theme_distribution_data,
  aes(
    x = percentage,
    y = theme_key,
    fill = srq
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    width = 0.65
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = scales::percent(
        percentage,
        accuracy = 0.1
      )
    ),
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 3.1,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ srq,
    ncol = 2,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = srq_palette
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(
      0,
      maximum_theme_percentage * 1.24
    ),
    breaks = scales::breaks_width(
      0.10
    ),
    labels = scales::percent_format(
      accuracy = 1
    ),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0)
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(
    labels = theme_distribution_labels
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Relative Distribution of Themes within Each Research Question",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Percentages represent the share of codes assigned ",
      "to each theme within its respective SRQ"
    ),
    x = "Percentage within the SRQ",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 15,
      hjust = 0.5,
      face = "bold"
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 10,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),

    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 11,
      face = "bold"
    ),

    axis.text.x = element_text(
      size = 9
    ),

    axis.text.y = element_text(
      size = 8.5
    ),

    axis.title.x = element_text(
      size = 10.5
    ),

    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none",

    panel.spacing = grid::unit(
      1,
      "cm"
    ),

    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 10,
      r = 35,
      b = 10,
      l = 10
    )
  )


print(theme_distribution_plot)

ggsave(
  filename = "figure_theme_distribution_within_srq.png",
  plot = theme_distribution_plot,
  width = 12,
  height = 14,
  dpi = 300
)
```
